# Normative box-model ledger and fixed-position reconciliation

Status: specified source extraction; implementation assertions are planned and unrun.
Source: retained CSS2.2 FPWD12April2016, box.html §§8.1–8.6 and the explicitly
identified §9.9.1 subset. This does not claim the rest of visuren or visudet was
extracted. R=rendering/parsing rule; D=definition field; U=undefined boundary;
P=permission. Every record supports CSS22-000008 or CSS22-000011; shorthand and
valid-value records also support000004–000006. Owners are architecture sections.

Property fields below are extracted directly from retained HTML definition tables
using the [retained generator](../tmp/layout-ledger-audit/build.py), preserving
value grammar and exceptions rather than paraphrasing the fields. Shared tables
are expanded per property; this is a record count, not a distinct test count.
Media fields are informative under chapter7 and excluded from normative fields.
The semantic prose was traversed separately; automated extraction is no semantic
verification claim. Value-type links still require their referenced algorithms.

## Region dispositions and source interpretation

- §8.1 definitions and painting ownership: explicit records above. Diagrams and
  descriptive image links illustrate the areas, not separate numeric algorithms.
- §8.2 is an example; no new requirement is derived from its sample HTML or pixels.
- §§8.3–8.5 property fields, value definitions and expansion/painting rules are
  recorded. Marked examples and notes are explanatory. In particular, collapse
  notes summarize consequences, and the note about special UI borders does not
  override this project's CSS-wins contract. Shorthand reset is independently
  owned by the cascade ledger even where the local explanation is in an example.
- §8.3.1 adjacency is a conjunction of eligibility, no separating material and an
  allowed edge pair. Transitive collapsed groups permit an empty chain with
  children to collapse through; the no-in-flow-children pair alone is not the
  whole algorithm. The explanatory note about positioning not affecting other
  boxes does not add an independently specified new layout formula.
- §8.6 is normative and requires visual edge placement. It does not replace
  Appendix E's painting order or fully define inline background positioning.
- §9.9.1 has an internal inconsistency: its explicit auto definition creates a
  context for fixed boxes, whereas its later generic overview and Appendix E
  auto grouping describe descendant escape. Selected interpretation under
  delegated authority: the explicit property rule controls context creation;
  fixed-auto contexts are atomic at level0, like other actual zero-level
  contexts. Apply generic auto descendant escape only to non-context-forming
  boxes. This is an identified reconciliation, not a claim the source is
  internally consistent. No modern property or trigger is imported.

## Remaining work and cases

Undefined percentage margin/padding cycles still need a deterministic library
policy owned by51/52. Exact dimension algorithms, clearance, phantom lines,
fragment splitting and table border transformations remain dependent on the
unextracted visuren/visudet/text/tables clauses. The checked-f32 path must preserve
negative collapse outcomes; no native margin wrapper or saturation shortcut is
qualified by these records. Property-table auto computed-value omissions (margin
fields say percentage or absolute length while the grammar allows auto) must be
read with §10.3's used-value algorithm; do not erase the auto variant on that
basis. General numeric and parser interpretations remain in their source ledgers.

Planned fixed-context case: a fixed auto sibling contains positioned z-index:99,
and a separate positioned sibling has z-index:1. The latter paints above the
entire fixed context. Change the first box to relative auto and its positioned
child participates in the parent context instead. Neither case was executed here.

## Source classification and selected scope

About §§1.2,1.3,1.5 and introductory tutorials/design principles are explicitly
informative. About §1.1 describes the relationship to prior CSS editions; it does
not import removed features. Its specimen property table is a documentation
template, not an additional property. Initial, inherited and computed table fields
retain the meanings supplied by their definitions and the cascade chapter.

The selected host parses the five page properties and preserves their cascade,
inheritance and computed values. It does not paginate. Page declarations remain a
separate context and never become element declarations. These are architecture
consequences of the existing parsing/applicability distinction in
[the property inventory](property-inventory.md), not a new printing commitment.
Actual parser and runtime behavior remains unqualified.

The canvas definition does not settle native-window backdrop transparency. Q273
remains pending in [questions](questions.md). Full imported-reference coverage,
source discrepancies and cross-clause interactions remain open.

# Normative ledger continuation — definitions and conformance boundaries

Status: inspected retained chapter3 text, including its scoped examples and notes.
CSS22-000030 through000070 supplement the earlier twelve §3.2 records without
replacing them. These are source definitions, obligations, permissions and scope
rules; they are not 41 implemented or passing CSS tests.

Source: [retained conform.html](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html), CSS22 FPWD
12 April 2016, fingerprinted in [source baseline](normative-source-baseline.md).
Each locator below names the anchor and direct paragraph/definition. Source
classification follows that region’s text: permissions remain permissions and
informative scope markers classify their contents rather than require rendering.

Common evidence status: specified, implementation unverified. Design owners are
numbered architecture sections; the source/capture, cascade, formatting, resource
and API contracts provide direction, not execution evidence. Applicability is
managed screen sources in Compile/Manual/Auto unless the row explicitly describes
a conditional role/device permission. Native platforms and both backends retain
the same source semantics; backend incapacity is not a scope exclusion.

| ID | Retained locator | Obligation, definition or permission | Owner | Planned semantic case |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CSS22-000030 | [§3 #defs](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#defs); Opening requirement-word paragraph | Interpret requirement words using RFC2119 even when lowercase. | 45 | FORCE: uppercase/lowercase wording retains the same requirement level. |
| CSS22-000031 | [§3 #defs](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#defs); Good-practice recommendation paragraph | Recommendations identified as good practice are non-normative; conformance does not require them. | 45 | SCOPE-RECOMMENDATION: classify scoped recommendations separately from normative should statements. |
| CSS22-000032 | [§3 #defs](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#defs); Deprecation paragraph | Deprecation alone does not remove conformance obligations; normative system colors remain required. | 50 | DEPRECATION: do not reject system colors because they are marked for future deprecation. |
| CSS22-000033 | [§3 #defs](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#defs); All sections paragraph | Sections and appendices are normative unless explicitly stated otherwise. | 45 | SCOPE-DEFAULT: preserve default force outside each explicit exclusion. |
| CSS22-000034 | [§3 #defs](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#defs); Examples and notes paragraph | Examples and notes are non-normative. | 45 | SCOPE-EXAMPLE: example content is not promoted into an additional authored requirement. |
| CSS22-000035 | [§3 #defs](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#defs); Figures paragraph | Figures are illustrations, not reference renderings unless explicitly designated. | 72 | ORACLE-FIGURE: require explicit reference status before pixel comparison is normative. |
| CSS22-000036 | [§3 #style-sheet](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#style-sheet); Definition and origins paragraph | A stylesheet specifies presentation; distinguish author, user and UA origins in cascade. | 49 | ORIGIN: identical declarations at distinct origins retain their cascade role. |
| CSS22-000037 | [§3 #valid-style-sheet](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#valid-style-sheet); Validity paragraph and final invalid definition | Valid CSS22 uses its grammar and only defined at-rules, property names and values; invalidity is level-specific. | 49 | VALIDITY: syntax acceptance alone does not establish valid property values. |
| CSS22-000038 | [§3 #valid-style-sheet](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#valid-style-sheet); Opening compatibility sentences | Valid CSS1 sheets remain valid CSS22 with possible semantic changes; not every CSS2 sheet is valid CSS22. | 49 | LEVEL: avoid treating CSS2 or later feature names as automatically valid CSS22. |
| CSS22-000039 | [§3 #source-document](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#source-document); Definition | The source represents an element tree; each element has a type name, optional attributes and possibly empty content. | 47 | SOURCE: captured element metadata remains separate from generated formatting boxes. |
| CSS22-000040 | [§3 #doclanguage](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#doclanguage); Definition | CSS describes presentation without changing underlying document-language semantics. | 47 | SEMANTICS: display changes do not change source parentage or declared source roles. |
| CSS22-000041 | [§3 #element](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#element); Definition | Elements are the source language’s primary syntactic constructs, whose names may be used by style rules. | 47 | TYPE: selector type matching uses registered source names, not Rust display labels. |
| CSS22-000042 | [§3 #replaced-element](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#replaced-element); First and final paragraphs | Replaced-element contents are outside the CSS formatting/rendering model; they may have intrinsic dimensions or ratio. | 52 | REPLACED: outer CSS sizing and separate resource rendering have distinct responsibilities. |
| CSS22-000043 | [§3 #replaced-element](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#replaced-element); Sensitive intrinsic-dimensions paragraph | UA may withhold intrinsic dimensions believed to leak sensitive information. | 52 | PRIVACY-DIMS: permission needs an explicit policy; no automatic missing-dimensions excuse. |
| CSS22-000044 | [§3 #intrinsic](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#intrinsic); First three sentences | Intrinsic dimensions come from the element, not surroundings; their discovery is outside CSS; in CSS22 only replaced elements have them. | 52 | INTRINSIC: do not confuse non-replaced content measurements with replaced intrinsic dimensions. |
| CSS22-000045 | [§3 #intrinsic](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#intrinsic); Raster resolution sentence | Raster images without reliable resolution information use one CSS px per source image pixel. | 62 | RASTER-SIZE: absent resolution metadata maps a20x10 raster to20px by10px intrinsic dimensions. |
| CSS22-000046 | [§3 #attribute](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#attribute); Definition | An attribute has a name and associated textual value. | 47 | ATTRIBUTE: preserve source text values for selector evaluation. |
| CSS22-000047 | [§3 #content](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#content); Definition | Source content may contain text and subelements; no content means empty; the containing element is their parent. | 47 | CONTENT: empty source content is distinguished from hidden or unpainted content. |
| CSS22-000048 | [§3 #ignore](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#ignore); First meaning and linked recovery sections | Parser ignoring discards precisely the portions prescribed by the applicable syntax recovery rule. | 49 | IGNORE-SYNTAX: invalid declaration recovery does not discard unrelated valid declarations. |
| CSS22-000049 | [§3 #ignore](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#ignore); Second meaning | Properties/values can be disregarded by applicability rules even when their syntax is valid. | 51 | IGNORE-APPLICABILITY: table-column font behavior is not implemented by marking font syntax invalid. |
| CSS22-000050 | [§3 #rendered-content](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#rendered-content); Definition | Rendered content follows styles and may include replacements, alternate text and generated items; replaced internal rendering is unspecified. | 56 | RENDERED: generated markers do not mutate source child lists. |
| CSS22-000051 | [§3 #doctree](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#doctree); Definition including root | Every source element has exactly one parent except the root, which has none. | 47 | TREE: reject shared/cyclic source parentage without confusing native implementation slots with elements. |
| CSS22-000052 | [§3 #child](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#child); Definition | A is B’s child exactly when B is A’s parent. | 47 | CHILD: source child selectors use immediate parentage. |
| CSS22-000053 | [§3 #descendant](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#descendant); Definition | Descendant is the recursive child relation. | 47 | DESCENDANT: deeper descendants match; the element itself does not become its own descendant. |
| CSS22-000054 | [§3 #ancestor](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#ancestor); Definition | Ancestor is the inverse descendant relation. | 47 | ANCESTOR: source ancestry is unchanged by anonymous box creation. |
| CSS22-000055 | [§3 #sibling](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#sibling); Definition | Siblings share a parent; preceding/following siblings are distinguished by document-tree order. | 47 | SIBLING: layout reordering does not change source sibling order. |
| CSS22-000056 | [§3 #preceding](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#preceding); Definition | A preceding element here is an ancestor or preceding sibling, as explicitly defined in this section. | 47 | PRECEDING: do not substitute a generic flattened traversal relation for this defined term. |
| CSS22-000057 | [§3 #following](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#following); Definition | Following element is the inverse of the preceding-element definition. | 47 | FOLLOWING: use the source-defined inverse relation. |
| CSS22-000058 | [§3 #author](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#author); Definition including authoring tool | Author writes documents/stylesheets; an authoring tool is a UA generating stylesheets. | 45 | ROLE-AUTHOR: Compile consumption does not by itself claim authoring-tool conformance. |
| CSS22-000059 | [§3 #user](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#user); Definition | User interacts with the UA and may supply a personal stylesheet expressing preferences. | 71 | ROLE-USER: user origin is preserved independently of author defaults. |
| CSS22-000060 | [§3 #user-agent](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#user-agent); Definition and following HTML/XHTML paragraph | UA interprets source and styles; XHTML-only support does not imply HTML-UA status for CSS conformance. | 45 | ROLE-UA: iced source mapping does not silently claim HTML parser behavior. |
| CSS22-000061 | [§3 #property](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#property); Definition | CSS properties are named rendering parameters assigned through specificity, cascade and inheritance. | 51 | PROPERTY: computed property assignment is distinct from whether a box paints it. |
| CSS22-000062 | [§3 #conformance](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#conformance); Exception list first item | A non-rendering stylesheet-reading application must respect general points1–3. | 72 | ROLE-VALIDATOR: a parser-only result is not evidence of rendering conformance. |
| CSS22-000063 | [§3 #conformance](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#conformance); Exception list second item | An authoring tool is required to output valid stylesheets. | 72 | ROLE-GENERATOR: apply only if an interface emits stylesheet source, not just binary artifacts. |
| CSS22-000064 | [§3 #conformance](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#conformance); Exception list third item, approximation sentence | A rendering UA may approximate values when required, subject to the actual-value rules. | 50 | ACTUAL: retain specified/computed values separately from a justified device approximation. |
| CSS22-000065 | [§3 #conformance](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#conformance); Device inability paragraph | A particular device’s inability to implement a feature does not itself imply non-conformance. | 70 | DEVICE: dependency/API absence is not silently equated to a physical-device limitation. |
| CSS22-000066 | [§3 #conformance](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#conformance); User stylesheet file paragraph, exemption | The file requirement exempts devices without any means of writing or specifying files. | 71 | FILE-EXEMPTION: file-capable native targets do not receive an invented exemption. |
| CSS22-000067 | [§3 #conformance](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#conformance); Same paragraph final sentence | UA may additionally expose other means of user preferences, such as a GUI. | 71 | PREFERENCES: GUI controls supplement the required native file interface. |
| CSS22-000068 | [§3 #conformance](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#conformance); Form controls and frames paragraph | CSS22 does not specify property applicability/styling for form controls and frames; UA application is permitted. | 61 | CONTROL: record the approved product control contract instead of attributing all internal behavior to CSS22. |
| CSS22-000069 | [§3 #errors](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#errors); Section3.3 paragraph | Error behavior is specified throughout CSS, including the linked parsing-error rules. | 49 | ERROR-ROUTING: preserve local required handling rather than one blanket fatal-error policy. |
| CSS22-000070 | [§3 #text-css](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#text-css); Section3.4 paragraph | Separate Internet stylesheets are byte message entities with encoding information; text/css represents an independent CSS document under the cited MIME/HTTP registration references. | 62 | ENTITY: preserve actual metadata and representation bytes for the CSS detection algorithm. |

## Lineage, interpretation and remaining work

The source-model rows support CSS22-000008; validity/recovery rows support000004–
000007; role/device/control rows qualify the applicability of000001–000012.
These parent/child relationships are traceability, not proof that every required
child or cross-property interaction is extracted. Referenced cascade, selectors,
actual values and error algorithms still require their own detailed records.

The chapter’s HTML source/tree example and its figure are informative under the
explicit example scope. No HTML parsing behavior is imported into the iced source
language from that example. The explanatory CSS1/CSS2 compatibility statements
are preserved without claiming a full older-version semantic comparison.

The device and native-control permissions do not reduce the user's approved
product requirements. Intrinsic-dimension suppression is a normative permission,
not an adopted policy or an invented security requirement. The raster1px rule
applies only when resolution information is unreliable; what constitutes reliable
format metadata remains the resource owner’s qualification work.

The definition of preceding element is narrower than a casual reading of all
prior nodes in document order. This ledger preserves the exact defined relation;
uses of different traversal terms elsewhere require their own context review.

[Message-entity reference review](css-message-entity-audit.md) covers the retained
RFC invocation boundaries. ISO8879 and the broader document-language/reference
closure remain tracked by [reference intake](normative-reference-register.md).
No unretained external definition is claimed as reviewed here. Chapter3 source
traversal is now represented by explicit records and informative dispositions,
but full reference and interaction closure is not asserted.

Total explicit CSS ledger records after this continuation: 70. That count is not
a denominator for all CSS requirements. The full normative extraction blocker
remains open, and no planned case in this file has run against a product parser.

## Scope and source reconciliation

Every direct section/subsection was traversed. The page-fragment/printing cases
in10.1 are excluded for screen output; the same containing-block and fixed
algorithms retain their screen cases. Marked notes, sample documents, illustrative
containing-block tables and CSS3 references do not introduce extra authored syntax.
The font-metric preference for OS/2 sTypoAscender/sTypoDescender then HHEA is a note,
so any adopted preference is a library policy, not a normative-only mandatory path.

The normal-block horizontal equation can yield a negative result for auto width
when fixed padding/borders exceed containing width. This ledger preserves the
equation and the declaration prohibition separately; it does not silently choose
a saturation algorithm. Review with numeric recovery and available-space policy.
The intrinsic-ratio constraint table includes divisions by w/h: zero intrinsic
sizes require a documented limiting/branch policy before implementation. The
comparison-row predicates must be selected as full simultaneous violations, not
naively first-matched single inequalities.

§10.6.5 step3 zeroes margins when bottom is auto, whereas the horizontal counterpart
checks either offset. With top auto, bottom specified, and both vertical margins
auto, the next equal-margin constraint still leaves more than one variable free.
The retained text alone does not specify a unique solution for this combination.
Record it as an unresolved solver interpretation, not a proven arbitrary result.
§10.7 invokes the replaced-both-auto constraint route without repeating10.4's
intrinsic-ratio condition; the no-ratio branch must be reconciled explicitly.

In §10.3.8 step5, “an auto left” means an auto value remaining, not exclusively the
left property. The immediately surrounding substitution sequence and equation
support this reading; distinguish it from the literal left property in other steps.

The height percentage fallback occurs at used-value calculation in this retained
baseline. Do not overwrite a computed percentage with auto, including when the
computed value is later inherited. Likewise min/max reruns do not overwrite actual
computed properties used by collapse/inheritance. Vertical absolute paired-auto
margins lack the horizontal negative-centering exception; sharing one solver must
preserve this axis-specific difference.

# Normative ledger continuation — stylesheet encoding

Status: inspected CSS22 §4.4 obligations; specified, implementation unverified.
Source: retained [syndata.html#charset](../tmp/css22/spec/syndata.html#charset),
fingerprinted in normative-source-baseline.md. IDs continue the twelve initial
records without reuse. All are children supporting CSS22-000004; source classification
is normative requirement/definition except the explicitly identified permissions
and recommendations. All apply to stylesheet intake in Compile, Manual and Auto.

Primary design owner: 49; collaborating owners: 62 for transport metadata, 64/65
for failure/publication, 66 for source coordinates and 72 for cases. Approved
design basis is section49's byte-first decode boundary. These source records do
not certify its unimplemented decoder or select an unreviewed charset library.

| ID | Precise §4.4 locator | Independently checkable obligation / permission | Required case and semantic assertion |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CSS22-000013 | Opening two paragraphs | Stylesheets are UCS character sequences; stored/transmitted encoding supports the US-ASCII character set | ENC-CHARACTERS: preserve decoded characters and original byte provenance |
| CSS22-000014 | Paragraph beginning “When a style sheet is embedded” | Embedded CSS shares its containing document encoding | ENC-EMBEDDED: supplied source-language encoding governs embedded input |
| CSS22-000015 | Ordered list of five priorities | Separate-file detection precedence is transport parameter, BOM/charset detection, linking metadata, referring source encoding, then UTF-8 | ENC-PRECEDENCE: conflicting candidates at each adjacent priority; apply subsequent BOM exceptions |
| CSS22-000016 | Paragraph beginning “Authors using an @charset” | Authored charset declaration occurs at the beginning, with only an appropriate BOM allowed before it | ENC-POSITION: space/comment before charset does not act as detection declaration |
| CSS22-000017 | Paragraph beginning “@charset must be written literally” | Detection spelling is literal lowercase prefix, double-quoted encoding name and semicolon; no escapes | ENC-LITERAL: case, quote, escape and delimiter variations |
| CSS22-000018 | Paragraph beginning “The name must be a charset name” | Name comes from IANA charset registry; preferred MIME names are recommended to authors | ENC-NAME: retained registry name/alias resolution; registry edition/input still needs intake |
| CSS22-000019 | Paragraph beginning “User agents must support at least” | UTF-8 support is mandatory | ENC-UTF8: valid multibyte input and source-coordinate mapping |
| CSS22-000020 | Paragraph beginning “If rule 1 above” and following five-row table | Generic transport UTF-8/16/32 is overridden by recognized initial BOM according to that table | ENC-TRANSPORT-BOM: every table row and conflicting generic transport label |
| CSS22-000021 | Paragraph beginning “If rule 1 yields” | Explicit-endian UTF-16BE/LE or UTF-32BE/LE plus BOM is an error; recover by ignoring the specified encoding and using the preceding table | ENC-ENDIAN-ERROR: diagnostic and recovered bytes agree |
| CSS22-000022 | Paragraph beginning “User agents must ignore any @charset” | Charset rules outside the beginning are ignored | ENC-LATE: retain later valid style declarations without changing decoder |
| CSS22-000023 | First detection-list item | Except for the specified detection rules, ignore charset rules | ENC-NONDETECTION: no ordinary cascade effect from charset |
| CSS22-000024 | Second detection-list item, before table | Recommended byte-prefix detection chooses first matching table row and shortest repetition for name bytes | ENC-PREFIX: overlapping prefixes and shortest terminating quote/semicolon |
| CSS22-000025 | Same item, “User agents may ignore entries” | Entries relevant only to unsupported encodings may be ignored | ENC-UNSUPPORTED-TABLE: supported-encoding registry controls admissible detection entries; permission is not arbitrary UTF-8 lossy decoding |
| CSS22-000026 | Detection table XX/YY explanation | Name bytes follow specified order and required ASCII transcoding where marked | ENC-NAME-BYTES: matched entries decode the actual name rather than raw-byte guessing |
| CSS22-000027 | Detection table final “analogous patterns” row | UA may add analogous patterns for supported encodings absent from the table | ENC-EXTENSION: any selected extension is separately recorded; none is assumed by this ledger |
| CSS22-000028 | Third detection-list item | For an “as specified” result, ignore stylesheet unless the chosen decoding yields an appropriate initial charset rule | ENC-REDECODE: mismatched declaration encoding, BOM incompatibility and newline in name cannot bypass validation |
| CSS22-000029 | Final paragraph before §4.4.1 | Ignore stylesheets in unknown encodings | ENC-UNKNOWN: no replacement-character reinterpretation; mode-specific diagnostic/build policy remains separate |

Source permissions and should-level recommendations preserve their original force;
recording them does not turn every table encoding into a mandatory decoder. Exact
table bytes remain in the retained source instead of a second hand-transcribed
copy. Malformed-byte recovery, supported charset catalogue/aliases, and the IANA
source are outstanding detailed design/intake work under 49/62. They must be
settled before decoder implementation and section74 closure.

No ENC case above has run against a product parser. Full §4 lexical/recovery
extraction, all other chapters and external reference dispositions remain open.

## Scope, interpretations and remaining qualification

§15.1 explains taxonomy limitations; no universal name-classification algorithm is
inferred. The generic-family sample font lists, weight-mapping examples, HTML-size
guidelines and sample rules are illustrative. They are not mandated bundled assets.
Naming heuristics and keyword-size recommendations remain distinct from compulsory
matching order and relative-weight tables. The system-font example says9-point but
then writes9px; use normative unit conversion, not that inconsistent example.

§15.7's property-specific em/ex rule resolves the broad root-relative wording in
§4.3.2: initial-font fallback supplies the missing parent basis for root font-size;
other root properties use the root computed font size, not an unrelated initial
font size. This is a recorded cross-clause interpretation. Actual ex metrics and
font-relative unit qualification remain with50/57 and their earlier decisions.

Matching remains specified per character; the architecture's shaping-safe cluster
fallback must be qualified against that obligation where a cluster spans fonts,
styles or source elements. HarfRust's bounded suite is not execution of these CSS
matching assertions. Monospace equality, emergency-font licenses, generic mapping,
synthetic small-caps/case behavior, system role snapshots, and all target discovery
remain dependencies. No bundle/OS role is claimed verified by reading CSS.

## Scope, quote interpretation and reference gaps

The opening describes two mechanisms: content on before/after and display:list-item.
Audio/braille presentation suggestions do not change the screen-only target scope.
Quote glyph tables and sample output are explicitly informative or examples, not
an exhaustive mandatory quote catalogue. Numbering/CSS3 references do not import
modern list properties. The note about replaced-element pseudo interaction identifies
incomplete definition; it does not choose a replacement-image overlay model.

§12.3.2's prose counts operations before the current occurrence but does not state
opening-versus-closing index timing clearly; the exhausted-pair wording also needs
care with zero-based indexing. Selected interpretation: opening selects at current
depth then increments; closing first decrements (unless at0) and selects at the
resulting depth. No-open/no-close perform only their depth operation. For nonempty
pairs, clamp pair index to last index; quotes:none emits nothing while preserving
operations. This preserves paired opening/closing levels; it is a recorded
interpretation, not an assertion that the retained prose is unambiguous.

The numbered-system labels do not supply complete Roman/Armenian/Georgian/Greek
algorithms, ranges or negative/zero conventions. Keep required reference/algorithm
qualification open. Previously approved decimal fallback in undefined ranges and
source-parent implicit list numbering remain library policy. A modern counter-style
reference can inform a documented policy without becoming authored CSS syntax.

## Remaining interaction work

Qualify counter scopes with repeated reset names, sibling boundaries, ungenerated
pseudos and hidden content; quote traversal with display suppression; first-letter
with generated content; image intrinsic failure and font changes; and inside markers
preceding before-pseudos. Outside marker painting order, floats, overflow hiding and
line-height choices must point to concrete policies. No counter/list/quote behavior
was executed here, and public generic image rendering does not close these cases.

Allocated 122 records, CSS22-001462–CSS22-001583.

## Q284 built-in counter algorithms

Selected ranges, retained symbol tables and exact formatting contracts are in
[the built-in counter contract](builtin-counter-style-contract.md). Eleven source
definitions and 97 Unicode character names are checked; a complete counter
formatter and text/marker integration remain unrun.

# Normative ledger — painting, visual effects, UI and media

Status: direct retained-source traversal completed locally after the parallel
attempt was interrupted. This ledger covers media.html, colors.html, visufx.html,
zindex.html and ui.html. It records source requirements, definitions, permissions
and explicit undefined cases, not product implementation or conformance tests.

Source baseline: CSS2.2 FPWD12April2016, fingerprinted in
[normative-source-baseline.md](normative-source-baseline.md). Every row includes
an anchor and a direct paragraph/table/step locator. D means normative definition;
R retains the prose's requirement force, including should and may where stated;
S denotes an explicit undefined/scope boundary. Conditional author/HTML/paged
statements retain their conditions rather than imposing an HTML parser on iced.

Common applicability: managed screen sources in all three modes, native targets
and both renderers. Device/source-language exceptions apply only where stated.
Property Media table fields are informative under §7.3 and are not counted as
normative property restrictions. Definition-table rows are split by field; planned
cases must check all alternatives of a referenced grammar or enumeration.

Every record has evidence status specified; implementation unverified. Primary
owners link through the numbered architecture index. Source extraction supplies
requirements to approved contracts and does not by itself approve an unchosen
policy. The named semantic assertions below are planned, not executed tests.

## Coverage and scope dispositions

Media: §7.1–7.3 direct prose and names are covered. HTML association and CSS
examples are illustrative. §7.3.1 explicitly declares itself informative, so its
group mapping table is not a separate normative requirement. Media descriptions
and each property's Media field are also explicitly informative. The Media Queries
note imports no newer query syntax or recovery rule into the selected CSS baseline.

Colors: §14.1 definition/prose, §14.2 canvas/background paragraphs, and every §14.2.1
property table and value/intrinsic-size paragraph are covered. Marked examples and
figures are not pixel oracles. The HTML author recommendation is non-normative;
the following conditional root/BODY propagation requirement is retained separately.
The visibility sentence explains the operative box-generation condition and has
no separate note-class wrapper; the ledger preserves that clarification.

Visual effects: §11.1 and its overflow examples, §11.1.1 value/propagation/scrollbar
rules, §11.1.2 shape/clip composition and §11.2 visibility are covered. The unmarked
satellite/scroller example is illustrative support for independently stated
containing-block exceptions. Future nonrectangular clip note and script examples
are informative; no scripting runtime or future clip shape follows.

Appendix E: E.1 definitions and every E.2 numbered/subnumbered branch are covered.
The text diagram and line-splitting note are illustrations. E.3 is explicitly
headed Notes and is treated as explanatory here; root single painting is independently
required in E.2/chapter14. Inline positioning remains expressly undefined in
chapter14, so E.3 does not supply a fabricated exact inline-background oracle.

UI: all §18.1 cursor values, §18.2 system-color definitions, §18.3 reference,
§18.4 outline tables/prose, §18.4.1 focus and §18.5 magnification are covered.
The SVG cursor example and linked SVG cursor element do not mandate that format.
System-color deprecation and same-outline-on-all-sides notes remain informative;
normative names/property grammars are retained independently. The 28 system names
are preserved individually, including the source's unusual ButtonHighlight wording.

## Verified source issues and design consequences

1. Media §7.3 says a non-identifier invalidates the statement, then an example
   uses screen,3D as though valid. Follow the normative malformed-media sentence;
   the example is explicitly scoped non-normative. Do not add modern recovery.
2. clip's bottom-auto explanatory link targets the right anchor, while its visible
   text and height/padding formula clearly say bottom. Use the stated vertical
   formula; retain the link defect as provenance rather than swapping axes.
3. Table overflow differs from ordinary scroll containers: all values except
   hidden act as visible on the table box. Root viewport propagation also changes
   the source element's used overflow to visible. These cases are explicit in60.
4. A hidden background-source element still generates boxes; display:none does
   not. Root canvas background propagation must not reuse ordinary hidden-paint
   suppression as its eligibility condition.
5. Appendix E's generic auto-positioned grouping needs reconciliation with the
   fixed-position/auto context rule in visuren. That other chapter has not been
   fully extracted here; no silent resolution is claimed.
6. Focus must be represented, but the mechanism is not fixed to outlines. Reconcile
   author outline:none and the CSS-wins contract explicitly; no undocumented
   forced outline or extra application UI is selected by this extraction.
7. Inline image positioning/tiling, ratio-only image positioning, outline overlap
   and cursor rectangle dimensions need identified library policies. A clear
   undefined boundary is not missing normative text and must not become a false
   CSS mandate. Existing product commitments remain binding even where CSS allows
   reduced device behavior, notably repository-owned inversion support.

## Q283 focus/cascade reconciliation

[Focus representation](focus-cascade-reconciliation.md) selects an ordinary UA-origin
:focus outline plus the host focus record. Honor winning author/user overrides;
do not add hidden out-of-cascade focus chrome. This follows the user's CSS-wins
requirement and records the interpretation/acceptance cases explicitly.

# Normative ledger continuation — selectors and cascade

Status: direct traversal of the retained chapters 5 and 6. CSS22-000185 through CSS22-000304 are centrally allocated; no predecessor is retired. These are source records and
planned semantic assertions, not implementation or executed conformance evidence.

The retained CSS 2.2 FPWD 12 April 2016 artifacts are
[selector.html](../tmp/css22/spec/selector.html), SHA-256
`ec9298b749956d9c897bed021d950543e6c481dde96a5d9a566aa67d77ba6e83`, and
[cascade.html](../tmp/css22/spec/cascade.html), SHA-256
`4c99129c83c24b19bd4da7ccc3777653cbb37790d1f1c6d02dd2c01cd1024638`.
These identities supplement the [source baseline](normative-source-baseline.md).
The extraction follows the [ledger protocol](normative-ledger-design.md) and
[definitions continuation](normative-definitions-ledger.md).

Every row inherits evidence status **specified; implementation unverified**.
Classification is D (normative definition), R (normative requirement, including
lowercase should), P (normative permission/constrained choice), or S (normative
scope/unspecified boundary). A slash indicates explicitly separated clauses in
one closely coupled record, not a change of requirement force. Planned cases are
oracles for future semantic fixtures; none has run against the product.

Applicability defaults to the managed semantic source tree captured from annotated
ordinary iced views, screen, Compile/Manual/Auto, every required native target and
both renderers. Text/formatting rows apply when their explicit eligible content
exists. Conditional HTML/XML/DTD/authoring rows say so; no iced HTML parser or DTD
is inferred. Backend/API limitations do not exclude a row. P records identify CSS
latitude, not a newly selected library policy. Existing user approvals, including
CSS-wins/defaults and source metadata policy, remain binding.

Design progress: the source/matching and cascade direction is approved in
[section 47](architecture-47-source-selectors.md), its
[kernel](source-selector-contract.md), and
[section 49](architecture-49-syntax-cascade.md). This extraction does not approve
new choices. Detailed property interactions and the explicit gaps below remain
unresolved pending their owner's audit. Owner numbers identify one accountable
[roadmap section](remaining-roadmap.md); `+` names cooperation. All rows depend on
CSS22-000030–000035's force/scope rules and source/value definitions as applicable.

## Selector records

Locators count prose by its identifying opening words, excluding example/notes
unless their scope is explicitly discussed. The chapter's summary table is mapped
again in the traversal register so its rows are not mistaken for unreviewed text.

| ID | Retained locator and class | Source rule and conditions | Owner / dependencies | Planned semantic assertion |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CSS22-000185 | [§5.1 #pattern-matching](../tmp/css22/spec/selector.html#pattern-matching), opening paragraph; D | A selector matches an element exactly when all its pattern conditions are true on the document tree. | 47; CSS22-000039–000057 | SEL-ALL: one false constituent prevents a match despite all other true constituents. |

# Normative ledger continuation — syntax, recovery and basic values

Status: retained source reviewed; requirements specified; implementation unverified.
This bounded audit covers CSS 2.2 §4.1–§4.3 inclusive, every paragraph, token
and macro table row, core grammar production, list item and scoped example/note.
It also covers §4.4.1, independently read after checking that the existing
[encoding ledger](normative-encoding-ledger.md) covers §4.4 only before §4.4.1.
That preceding encoding-detection region is not duplicated here.

Source identity: retained [syndata.html](../tmp/css22/spec/syndata.html),
CSS22 FPWD 12 April 2016, with exact artifact identity/hash in
[source baseline](normative-source-baseline.md). Locators below use local anchors,
named paragraphs/rows/productions and retained HTML line numbers. Line numbers
supplement the anchor and prose locator; they are not identity keys.

CSS22-000071 through CSS22-000184 were allocated centrally at integration. No existing record is
retired. Syntax/recovery rows support CSS22-000004–000007 and CSS22-000048;
value/application rows support CSS22-000005–000006 and CSS22-000061.
Dependencies and interactions among rows remain necessary even where each row
has its own semantic assertion. These children do not close those broad parents.

Common fields apply to every row: source kind is CSS22; design progress is
**unresolved** for detailed algorithm/qualification, with approved roadmap owner
contracts providing direction only; evidence status is **specified**, with no
product parser, renderer, revision, executed case or target run supplied. Tests
below are **planned semantic assertions**, not test results. The common case
prefix is `SYN-` followed by the original extraction sequence number. Every row has one primary
numbered roadmap owner; 72 cooperates on verification, 66 on source coordinates,
49 on parsing, 50 on typed values, and the specific reference owners below on
external dependencies. No new policy or dependency selection is approved here.

Applicability: all managed stylesheet input in Compile, Manual and Auto, all
native targets and both backends. Value realization additionally applies when
that value participates in a supported screen formatting/resource context;
syntax and recovery still apply when a property or medium has no screen effect.
Rows expressly qualified as author/preprocessor/device roles apply only to those
roles; they do not assert that this library emits stylesheets. Device capability
or a missing dependency is not a blanket exclusion. Each row's open issues are
the common implementation/evidence gap plus any numbered issue cited below;
“reference review” is not an assertion that a target's contents were read here.

Force notation: **D** normative definition/constraint, **M** mandatory outcome,
**S** should/recommendation (retains its force), **P** permission/constrained
choice, **U** explicitly undefined behavior boundary. Informative notes/examples
are disposed separately. A single row may describe a small exhaustive lexical
family; its planned case must exercise every listed alternative and boundary.

## Core syntax and token tables

All locators in this table are under
[§4.1.1 #tokenization](../tmp/css22/spec/syndata.html#tokenization), except
where the linked §4.1 anchor is supplied. Exact regular expressions and grammar
bytes stay authoritative in the retained tables/pre block; paraphrases below do
not replace them. Case handling depends on CSS22-000108; escaping on CSS22-000110–CSS22-000118.

## Open source issues and verification gaps

I1. §4.1 L89–92 calls Appendix G's grammar normative; the retained appendix is
explicitly scoped non-normative in its opening paragraph,
[grammar.html](../tmp/css22/spec/grammar.html) L40, independently checked here.
This file preserves both claims. Resolving authority requires recorded source
comparison, not treating a convenient parser grammar as automatically binding.

I2. The lexical paragraph expressly says longest match but does not independently
spell out equal-length tie-breaking or Lex case configuration. The table order,
ASCII case rule and known token overlaps need explicit algorithm review; claiming
that a library's default token priority matches this source would be unverified.

I3. URI and BAD_URI unquoted character classes differ in their literal retained
expressions. This audit deliberately references the exact bytes instead of
normalizing them into one modern URL grammar. Test every class boundary and
longest-match interaction before selecting a tokenizer implementation.

I4. §4.1.1 `num` L166 expressly permits an exponent, whereas §4.3.1 number prose
L897–901 enumerates only integer/fraction decimal forms. Token recognition and
property-value validity are distinct, so preserving exponent tokens without
claiming exponent <number> validity is a viable interpretation to evaluate.
Recommended interpretation for owner 49: retain the broader lexical NUMBER
recognition, then validate each property against its value grammar, as required
by §4.1.8 and the existing §3.2 ledger. This separates the two explicit source
stages without adding authored <number> forms. It remains a proposed detailed
interpretation, not an approved resolution or verified parser behavior.

I5. Numeric escape zero prohibition and literal U+0000 undefined behavior do not
supply a full invalid-scalar algorithm. Out-of-range replacement is a permission,
not a universal requirement. Immediate-EOF backslash wording also needs checking
against quoted-string BAD_STRING and mandatory construct closure. No modern CSS
preprocessing/replacement convention is silently adopted.

I6. Declaration prose requires escaping semicolons outside strings, while core
block/unused productions can consume semicolons in nested constructs for parsing
and recovery. Core consumption must not be confused with accepted property value
syntax; precise normative/property boundaries need qualification.

I7. §4.3.2 L1001–1004 broadly says root em/ex refer to the property's initial
value; preceding em/ex paragraphs provide explicit font-size exceptions. A
contextual reading for root font-size would avoid overriding root margin's
computed-font-size basis, but the linked font-size/initial-value sections must be
reviewed before adopting that reading. Additional bounded reading of
[fonts.html #propdef-font-size](../tmp/css22/spec/fonts.html#propdef-font-size),
L675–688 and L767–769, confirms the initial medium/absolute-length computed
value and explicitly assigns em/ex on all other properties to the current
element, while font-size uses the parent. This supports recommending the
root-initial exception only for font-size resolution. The prose also loosely
describes ex in terms of computed font size; the precise x-height definition
in §4.3.2 must remain operative. This is proposed reconciliation, not a new
font chapter extraction or an approved test oracle for every root property.

I8. Recommendations/permissions for negative unsupported lengths, unknown
resources, color fidelity/gamut and unsupported values preserve their conditions.
They require concrete product policy and do not remove mandatory property,
parser, source or backend evidence obligations. Color gamut/transfer decisions
also depend on retained external definitions and target capability evidence.

All 114 records are source extraction with planned checks. They do not
claim 114 implemented tests, coverage of every CSS chapter, complete reference
closure, successful backend runs, or product conformance. No production files,
dependency selection, tests, commits or pushes are part of this artifact.

## Q277 interpretation update

[Grammar reconciliation](grammar-authority-reconciliation.md) supersedes the
earlier unresolved architecture choice in I1: chapter4's explicit token/character
and recovery rules take priority, with AppendixG a compatible grammar aid. The
source contradiction is still disclosed. I4's separation between broad lexical
recognition and decimal property-value validation is selected. I2 tie-breaking,
I3 URI boundaries and I5 invalid-scalar/EOF work remain open. Q271 already
resolved I7's root font-size interpretation in the font ledger.

## Q278 scanner continuation

[Scanner qualification](scanner-contract-qualification.md) records a retained Lex
priority reference, a selected explicit tie policy and five passing Rust probe
tests. I2 now has a priority interpretation; I3 has measured URI/BAD_URI overlaps
and prefix boundaries. Whole-parser recovery and invalid-scalar/EOF integration
remain open; earlier unqualified status statements are historical.

## Q279 scalar continuation

[CSS scalar boundary](css-scalar-boundary-review.md) selects stage-specific handling
for literal NUL, zero/surrogate/out-of-range numeric escapes and noncharacters,
with retained candidate Unicode17 definitions. I5 remains open for EOF context
and execution of the integrated decoder/parser cases.

## Q280 BAD_URI exception

[The longer-match regression](bad-uri-continuation-reconciliation.md) demonstrates
that I3 also requires a character-class reconciliation. Select AppendixG's narrower
baduri1 class as the explicit exception to Q277, retaining the other chapter4
macros. Q278's tie priority alone is not sufficient. Six bounded probe tests pass;
whole-parser recovery and EOF integration remain open.

## Q285 EOF/string interpretation

The [EOF reconciliation](eof-string-reconciliation.md) selects logical closure
with a final literal string backslash and preserves newline-error recovery.
Twenty-two bounded Rust assertions pass. This settles the named I5 interpretation;
whole-stylesheet recovery, URI EOF and diagnostic integration remain unqualified.

## Q286 declaration/recovery boundary

[Declaration reconciliation](declaration-recovery-reconciliation.md) distinguishes
accepted property values from nested tokens consumed only for recovery. Specific
URI token syntax retains internal semicolons as URI data. This selects the named
I6 interpretation; whole-parser recovery cases remain unrun.

The introduction describes table structure and shows HTML examples; no HTML source
semantics are automatically assigned to iced elements. §17.2 print header/footer
repetition is outside screen rendering. Its explicit first-header/footer ordering
specializes §17.5's general source-row-order statement; selector order is unchanged.

not a different baseline. Diagram/sample outputs elsewhere are not pixel oracles.

until §17.5.3 is a suggested algorithm. Section55 adopts that recipe as policy:

## Source tensions and architecture consequences

The table wrapper receives position/float/margins/offsets, while the generic
noninherited-property split places z-index on the inner table. Reconcile this with
positioned applicability and fixed-auto context creation before a final stacking
oracle is claimed. The property split alone does not specify the entire host paint
bridge. Caption example text referring to the table parent width likewise must not
override the normative wrapper width and ordinary caption containing-block rules.

Empty-cells hide is not purely a paint switch: a wholly empty hidden row has zero
height and one-sided vertical spacing. Its cell mask exposes the table background
through intermediate row/column layers. Visibility collapse instead retains prior
grid sizing constraints, removes occupied tracks and clips crossing spans.

For border conflicts retain original style priority; only then map collapsed inset
to ridge painting and outset to groove painting, exactly as retained §17.6.3 states.
Other remembered standards/browser mappings are not silently substituted. A future
comparison may document a source discrepancy, but does not change this baseline.

## Remaining policy and evidence

Still link concrete policies for overlapping spans, extra fixed-layout columns,
auto-width fixed permission, collapsed background bounds, odd-pixel shared borders,
row-group/percentage heights and wrapper stacking. Source registered spans and
anonymous repair must preserve out-of-flow containing-block selection. Actual grid,
renderer, editable-cell and multi-target cases remain unrun; extracted obligations
alone do not close section74 or demonstrate a CSS table implementation.

## Scope and cross-clause review

§16.3 introduces decoration subsections without an extra standalone algorithm.
§16.6.2 is an explicit bidi/whitespace example; do not derive an independent
universal two-space oracle from its particular markup. Other marked examples
illustrate the recorded rules. §16.6.3's combining sentence uses should and its
cross-element first-letter example illustrates that recommendation. Keep this
force distinct from the selector's mandatory applicable first-letter rules.

The decoration visibility note identifies an undefined visible-child case under
a hidden decorated ancestor; it does not select a CSS3 resolution. Constant line
thickness/color still applies to the defined propagation cases. The optional blink
exemption invokes UAAG as an example of satisfying a checkpoint, not incorporation
of every UAAG requirement. See the invocation register for exact reference scope.

The control-character paragraph's U+202x wording is broader than only the named
bidi embedding controls, and newer Unicode adds further controls outside that
range. The paragraph alone does not establish the modern character-set mapping.
Reconcile exact controls with approved Unicode17 analysis before implementation;
retain source scalars and diagnostic/source positions throughout normalization.
BCP47 and Unicode casing/word boundaries still require invocation-specific audits.

## Architecture consequences and remaining policies

Preserve a logical source stream, normalized stream, pre-collapse break positions,
collapsed rendering stream and shaped cluster mapping. These are distinguishable
stages, not necessarily five allocated copies. A one-pass per-widget string trim
cannot preserve the required cross-inline collapse and first-letter/combining
relationships. The editor bridge must retain original text for messages/copy and
map visual hit/caret positions through these transformations.

Explicit library choices remain for script-dependent LF conversion, optional
pre-wrap trailing collapse, letter/word spacing algorithms, justification,
capitalization word boundaries, hidden-decoration/table propagation, and additional
newline recognition. Existing approved choices take precedence when matched to
these exact clauses; this extraction does not silently overwrite them. Public
text/editor probes have not executed this ledger or closed Unicode/IME feasibility.

## Region dispositions and inconsistencies

§§9.1–9.7 and9.10 semantic prose and all ten previously unallocated property
fields are represented above. §9.2.3 is a numbering placeholder referring run-in
to CSS3, which remains outside the authored property grammar. §9.8 is an explicit
series of examples, with diagrams explicitly not reference renderings. Its inline
clear example cannot override the block-level applicability in §9.5.2. Nor does
its multiline positioned-inline diagram override §10.1's undefined boundary.
Marked notes/examples elsewhere illustrate rather than establish new algorithms.
Paged-media fixed repetition/clipping and no-pagination clauses are excluded from
screen behavior, but remain identified at §9.3.1/§9.6.1; this exclusion does not
remove parsing of position:fixed. References to other media do not broaden targets.

§9.9.1 is already represented by CSS22-000788–000799 in the box ledger and the
Appendix E ledger. Its seven-phase overview is not a second contradictory paint
algorithm. Q268 preserves actual fixed-auto contexts and the explicit property
creation rule. Other future stacking triggers remain outside the CSS2.2 grammar.

§9.10's inline-effect prose says override; its property grammar and value definition
say bidi-override. Use bidi-override and reject bare override. This is a recorded
source reconciliation. Author guidance about limiting bidi overrides is not an
instruction to ignore valid author declarations under this project's CSS-wins rule.
Conditional HTML/DTDs do not assign fictitious HTML attributes to iced sources.

The text claims a Unicode embedding limit of61. Retained
[UAX9 revision51](../tmp/unicode-reference/tr9-51.html) lines704–718 instead specifies
max_depth125 and says this has held since6.3.0. Under Q195/Q196's selected latest-
supported route, do not impose61 merely from that explanatory warning. The actual
qualified Unicode engine/version must govern its depth/overflow rules; importing
that algorithm does not enable CSS isolation or modern authored bidi keywords.
Full invocation/edition and implementation qualification remains N-REFERENCES and
D-QUALIFICATION, not a claimed completed Unicode audit.

## Delegated policy choices and remaining dependencies

Select the first permitted clearance algorithm: max(clear-lowest-float amount,
preserve-hypothetical-top amount). Negative and zero clearance remain possible;
clearance existence and magnitude are separate state. For same-BFC float avoidance
by a table/replaced/new-BFC block, preserve its category-computed width and try
adjacent placement only if that width fits; otherwise clear below the relevant
preceding floats. Do not take the optional arbitrary width reduction. Its precise
static-position/width interaction still needs §10's extraction.

Other undefined cases (relative table-internal positioning, negative-margin float
placement, root list-item choice, percentage cycles) remain explicit policy work.
Root static/float-none permissions must not be silently chosen through native
widget limitations. Clearance, anonymous boxes, bidi and BFC geometry assertions
remain unrun; the chapter10 size/line-height solvers and text/table algorithms are
required dependencies. This extraction does not close N-CLAUSES.

# Normative ledger — initial records

Status: initial source extraction using the protocol approved in Q194.
The IDs and record format are adopted. This is not a complete CSS
ledger, completed implementation audit, or conformance result.

Common source for the records below: retained CSS 2.2, First Public Working Draft
12 April 2016, [§3.2](../tmp/css22/spec/conform.html#conformance). Exact file hash is
in [normative-source-baseline.md](normative-source-baseline.md). All rows are
CSS 2.2 source obligations; none imports newer authored syntax.

## Initial source records

| ID | Precise locator within §3.2 | Independently checkable obligation | Applicability | Primary roadmap owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CSS22-000001 | General conformance list, item 1 | Recognize at least one CSS 2.2 media type. | This project selects screen under Q006. | 49 |
| CSS22-000002 | General list, item 2, first sentence | Attempt retrieval of associated stylesheets appropriate to recognized media. | Applicable associated stylesheet inputs; acquisition stage depends on mode. | 62 |
| CSS22-000003 | General list, item 2, second sentence | When not all associated stylesheets can be retrieved, display using retrievable ones. | Rendering case; distinguish runtime behavior from approved Compile acquisition failure policy. | 65 |
| CSS22-000004 | General list, item 3, first two sentences | Parse stylesheets according to CSS 2.2, recognizing its at-rules, blocks, declarations, and selectors. | All managed stylesheet input. Needs detailed syntax child records. | 49 |
| CSS22-000005 | General list, item 3, supported-property value sentences | Accept valid values for properties applicable to supported media. | Per-property applicability; missing implementation is not an unknown-property exemption. | 49 |
| CSS22-000006 | General list, item 3, invalid-value clause | Ignore declarations whose property values are invalid. | Apply the specified recovery boundary; requires property/syntax child records. | 49 |
| CSS22-000007 | General list, item 3, final sentence | Ignore rules applying to unsupported media types. | Screen-only output; syntax handling remains separately required. | 49 |
| CSS22-000008 | General list, item 4 | Assign each element a value for every property according to definitions, cascade, and inheritance. | Managed source tree and property applicability. Needs property and interaction children. | 51 |
| CSS22-000009 | General list, item 5 | Permit user selection among alternate stylesheet sets when supplied by the source document. | Conditional on source-provided sets; source/API mapping remains under design. | 71 |
| CSS22-000010 | General list, item 6 | Permit the user to disable author stylesheet influence. | All supported modes, preserving origins in Compile artifacts. | 71 |

## Design and evidence attached to these records

For all twelve records, source classification is normative and source text was
inspected locally. Evidence status is `specified` at the obligation level;
implementation and execution are unverified. Detailed algorithms and child records
are not implied by that status. These IDs do not constitute a coverage count
for all of CSS.

| 000001, 000007 | Q006; sections 4/14 | Media lists/import contexts; applicable and unsupported media cases. | Full media/source-clause extraction and parser fixtures. |
| 000002, 000003 | Sections 9/15–19 | Acquisition reasons, relative imports, missing resource and retained-active cases, mode-specific build behavior. | Detailed resolver/publication contracts and mode integration evidence. |

The case families are verification planning inputs, not existing test names or
executed results. Each record must acquire concrete cases and evidence through
its owner. Architecture decisions cited here establish direction, not product
support.
